column4: ~/proj/prompts/reports/SESSION-REVIEW-LEAVES-1.md item 1. Two findings, both fixed. ROTATION-PG-LITERAL-SCS-OFF (medium): QuoteLiteral emitted a plain quote-doubled literal, so on a Postgres server/database/role with standard_conforming_strings=off a caller-supplied on-demand rotation value with a backslash-quote broke out and ran a second statement over the simple query protocol; now an E-string with backslashes doubled. Proof: internal/rotation/quote/review_leaves_test.go:TestQuoteLiteral_SafeWithStandardConformingStringsOff (server-model lexer, both scs settings; FuzzPostgresQuoting now decodes through the same lexer instead of mirroring the encoder) and internal/rotation/postgres_scs_off_postgres_test.go:TestQuoteLiteral_StandardConformingStringsOff_Postgres (real server, red on main: 2 statements ran). ROTATION-PREFIX-NONASCII-BOUNDARY (low): PrefixAllowed counted bytes >= 0x80 as a segment boundary, so allowed_refs myapp admitted myappé_admin; pinned by :TestPrefixAllowed_NonASCIIIsNotABoundary. Tried without finding: QuoteIdentifier needs no scs handling (identifiers have no backslash escapes); refs over 63 bytes are truncated by Postgres to a name that still carries the allowed prefix; QuoteMySQLString multibyte (GBK/SJIS 0x5c trail byte) and NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES value drift need a backslash or quote in the ref, which core.validateRotationRef rejects, and the MySQL password is a bound parameter; ValidateAzureRef: every Graph URL uses url.PathEscape, a ref of dots needs an allowed prefix of dots. Not covered: ValidateAzureRef does not enforce the bare-GUID shape its error message names (backslash and non-ASCII pass layer two; layer one rejects backslash)
